meta.title: Dawrak | An assistant that books clinic and salon appointments
meta.description: Dawrak takes text and voice messages in Arabic and its dialects, books the appointment and puts it in the owner's calendar, then sends reminders. Try a demo clinic.

hero.h1: A customer sends a voice note. The booking lands in your calendar.
hero.lead: Dawrak is an assistant that answers your clinic's or salon's customers in their own dialect, understands voice and text, and books the right slot step by step. Once confirmed, the appointment appears in the owner's calendar.
hero.note: A portfolio project with fictional data. The demo is free and needs no sign-up.
hero.sample: The chat and calendar here are a scripted example, not a real customer.
hero.transcript: "Hello, I'd like to book a dental check-up on Sunday, after the afternoon prayer."
hero.transcriptOriginal: «السلام عليكم، عايزة أحجز كشف أسنان يوم الأحد بعد العصر»
hero.m2: Hi Mona, I got your voice note. A dental check-up on Sunday, {day}. Would you like Dr. Hisham Al-Gohary?
hero.m3: Yes, but later in the afternoon if possible
hero.m4: Available with the doctor this afternoon:
hero.m6: Booked. You'll get a reminder by email two hours before.
hero.composer: Type a message or record your voice
hero.calFoot: After confirmation the customer gets the details, then two email reminders: 24 hours and 2 hours before the appointment.

how.title: Booking from the form: four steps on a phone
how.lead: Every clinic has its own booking page. The customer picks from a clear form, or lets the assistant do it in chat. The result is the same.
how.s1d: Duration and price show before any tap.
how.s2d: A specific doctor or stylist, or "any available" and the system picks the earliest free time.
how.s3d: Only genuinely free times appear, following each provider's hours and time off, with the Hijri date beside the Gregorian one.
how.s4d: Name and mobile number; email is optional. If the clinic asks for a deposit, the slot is held until it is paid.

assistant.title: An assistant that answers from the clinic's own data and books for you
assistant.lead: It reads and listens. It does not invent prices or times: every figure comes from the clinic's services, schedules and documents.
assistant.f1d: The owner uploads PDFs, text or FAQs. The assistant searches them and answers only from what it finds. If it finds nothing, it says it does not know.
assistant.f2d: It shows free times, summarises the booking and asks for an explicit yes before acting. Changes and cancellations cover appointments made in that same chat.
assistant.f3d: Customers record up to 25 seconds in the widget. It understands Modern Standard Arabic plus Gulf and Egyptian dialects, and reads the details back in text before confirming.
assistant.f4d: Arabic or English, and in the customer's own dialect when they write casually.
assistant.chanD: The assistant works inside the chat widget on the clinic's page. WhatsApp is planned: the code that maps WhatsApp messages onto the same assistant is written but not connected and does not run yet.
assistant.priceCap: A price question, answered from the clinic's documents
assistant.q1: How much is teeth whitening? Is there a family discount?
assistant.a1: Whitening at Al-Nada clinic is SAR 850 per session, from the uploaded price list. I found no family discount in the documents. Shall I book you in?
assistant.a2: Tomorrow after sunset with Dr. Hisham: 7:00 PM or 7:30 PM. Which do you prefer?
assistant.q3: I've had a small swelling on my gum for two days. Can I take the antibiotic I have at home?
assistant.a3: That is a medical question for the doctor and I can't answer it. I can book you a check-up with Dr. Hisham if you like.
assistant.handoffNote: Handing a chat over to front-desk staff is planned and not built yet. Today staff can read conversations in the dashboard but cannot reply to them.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Does Dawrak's assistant replace the front desk?
faq.a1: No. Dawrak's assistant handles booking, rescheduling, cancelling and questions that the clinic's own documents cover, and declines anything else. Staff can read conversations in the dashboard, but handing a chat over to a staff member to answer is planned and not built yet.
faq.a2: Dawrak's interface is in Arabic and English. The assistant replies in the customer's language and understands Modern Standard Arabic plus Gulf and Egyptian dialects, in text and voice.
faq.q3: How do deposits work in Dawrak?
faq.a3: Each clinic sets a deposit per service. After booking, the customer pays on Moyasar's secure page within 15 minutes, or the slot is released. The demo runs in test mode and charges nothing.
faq.a4: Not yet. Today Dawrak's assistant works inside the chat on the clinic's website page. A WhatsApp connection is planned, and preparatory code exists without being switched on.
faq.q5: Is each clinic's data separate from other clinics' data in Dawrak?
faq.a5: Yes. In Dawrak every record belongs to one clinic, and security rules in the database stop one clinic's staff from reading another clinic's data, whatever the front-end code does.
faq.a6: Dawrak is a portfolio project, not a live commercial service. The clinics, names and numbers in the demo are fictional, and nothing you type in the demo reaches anyone.

Facts.name: Dawrak
Facts.description: Dawrak is an Arabic-first appointment booking system for clinics and salons. Customers book through a booking form or a chat assistant that understands Arabic and English, in text and voice notes, and the appointment appears in the owner's calendar.
Facts.status: Dawrak is a portfolio project with fictional demo clinics, not a live commercial service.
does: Each clinic or salon gets its own public booking page with services, durations, prices and opening hours.
A chat assistant on that page books, reschedules and cancels appointments made in the same chat, and answers questions from the clinic's own uploaded documents. It declines medical questions.
Customers can record voice notes of up to 25 seconds. The assistant understands Modern Standard Arabic and Gulf and Egyptian dialects.
Appointments show in an owner dashboard with a calendar, services, staff, customers, conversations and revenue.
Customers get two email reminders, 24 hours and 2 hours before the appointment, and a private link to cancel or move it.
Clinics can ask for a deposit per service, paid on Moyasar's payment page (test mode in the demo). An unpaid slot is released after 15 minutes.
Dates show in the Hijri (Umm al-Qura) and Gregorian calendars side by side. The interface is right to left in Arabic and left to right in English.
Every clinic's data is separated by database security rules.
planned: Planned: connecting the assistant to WhatsApp. Today it works only in the website chat.
Planned: handing a chat over to front-desk staff. Today staff can read conversations but cannot reply to them.
Planned: reminders by SMS or WhatsApp. Today reminders are sent by email only.
